title: Governed Deployment Gateways: RBAC & Approval Flows for Model Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an approval and change-management layer for model production rollouts that integrates with canary/A-B/shadow traffic tooling. Deliverables: RBAC controls for who can create/approve rollouts, an auditable sign-off flow surfaced in the Console, immutable audit logs for each rollout decision, and a configurable auto-rollback policy that requires explicit sign-off to disable. This is targeted at customers using Dedicated and Private deployments but must be available for Hosted API customers with enterprise plans.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI exposes a ‘Create Rollout’ flow where the creator selects deployment mode (canary/A-B/shadow) and attaches required approvers
RBAC rules allow role-based gating: Draft rollout creation allowed by 'model-operator' role; only 'release-admin' or designated approvers can approve and promote
Every state transition (created -> approved -> promoted -> rolled-back) writes an immutable audit entry including actor, timestamp, reason, and related GitHub PR/Change ID

Auto-rollback policy can be configured per-rollout with thresholds (error-rate, latency, quality-regression) and a configurable 'grace period' before rollback; policy triggers are visible in rollout timeline
Audit log export available (CSV/JSON) covering the last 90 days and queryable by customer org id
E2E test: simulate a canary that breaches latency SLO and verify auto-rollback triggers and corresponding audit entries and notifications
rollout_plan: 1) Phase 0 (design): finalize UX wireframes and RBAC matrix. 2) Phase 1 (backend): implement approval API, audit-log schema, and hooks into existing canary runner. 3) Phase 2 (Console): add UI for creating rollouts and viewing timeline. 4) Phase 3 (integration): connect to Dedicated control plane and Private deploy workflows. 5) Phase 4 (pilot): enable for two enterprise customers and run three staged rollouts. Rollback tests included in pilot.
rbac_matrix: Roles proposed: model-operator (create draft, view), release-admin (approve/promote/force-rollout), auditor (view-only, export audit logs), security-operator (can enable emergency rollback). Approvals can be single-signature or require a gate with multiple approvers. Role membership is backed by SSO groups and mapped to org/team IDs.
audit_requirements: Audit entries must include: rollout_id, change_set (model id + version + config), actor (SSO ID), action, timestamp (ISO8601), justification (free-text), linked artifacts (GH PR / Confluence / eval-run ID), pre- and post-metrics snapshot (latency p50/p95, error-rate, eval-quality delta). Logs stored in write-once append store and retained per customer retention policy (default 90 days). Exports must be signed and checksummed for compliance audits.
signoff_workflow: Support both pre-approve and post-mortem signoffs. Default flow: creator opens rollout -> selects approver list -> optional automated evaluation gates (smoke tests, eval-score threshold) -> approver(s) receive notification with one-click approve/reject in Console and email. If rejected, rollout enters 'Blocked' with required remediation notes. Emergency path: 'security-operator' can bypass normal flow to initiate an immediate rollback; all bypasses must produce a high-priority audit entry and trigger a required retrospective within 3 business days.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- We chose lightweight in-Console approvals rather than heavy ticket integration (Jira) to reduce latency for small teams; we will add Jira links in 'linked artifacts'.
- Immutable audit log chosen over mutable comments to satisfy compliance for enterprise customers; accepts higher storage cost.
- Multi-approver gates implemented as quorum (N of M) rather than unanimous to avoid stalls for large orgs.
open_questions: Should approval notifications live in Slack for faster response or only email/Console (Slack integration planned in Phase 3)?
What default retention should we set for audit logs for enterprise customers (90 days vs 1 year)?
Edge case: if the model variant is pulled due to security vulnerability, should approval flows allow automatic revocation of pending rollouts?
